steps.name: Partitions of 3 — Schur–Weyl basis at A=1
steps.operation: By Schur–Weyl duality, the Markov-trace decomposition for an A=1 atom (n = 3·A = 3) sums over partitions λ ⊢ 3.  The three partitions are (3), (2,1), (1,1,1) with frame dimensions f_λ = 1, 2, 1.

steps.name: Trivial rep χ^(3)_q on proton braid word
steps.operation:
The trivial rep λ=(3) is 1-dimensional.  Each generator σ_i acts as multiplication by +q (Hoefsmit recipe in the 1-cell column).  For the proton's 6-crossing word T_w_p, χ^(3)_q(T_w_p) = q^{n_+ − n_−} where n_± count the σ vs σ⁻¹ appearances.  All proton crossings are positive σ → χ^(3)_q(T_w_p) = q^6.

[PREMISE CONTRADICTED BY THE PRODUCER -- flagged 2026-08-30, bean qou-1ucq, NOT repaired.] This step's premise that the proton word has 6 crossings and that they are ALL POSITIVE sigma is false against the live producer. Measured: `atom_braid_word_3A(1, 0, include_inter=False)` returns 11 letters, {sigma: 6, sigma^-1: 3, averaged: 2} -- confirmed independently by `canonical_braid_crossings.classify_crossing` and by reading h = 0.20906029879563932 off the returned d-values, which is h(q) at the proton pin to float64. On the canonical element the one-dimensional characters are therefore sigma^6 * (sigma - h)^3 * (sigma - h/2)^2, giving chi^(3) = q(q^2 + 1)^2 / 4, not q^6 -- a ratio of (q^2 + 1)^2 / (4 q^5). This is the same legacy-convention defect the neutron assembly chain already flags at its own step 4, and it was UNFLAGGED here. NOT re-derived: correcting it changes the value this chain reports, which is a compute change rather than a documentation one. TERMINOLOGY (bean qou-1ucq, 2026-08-30): these letters are NOT crossings. `atom_braid_word_3A` returns Hecke elements c*sigma_g + d*1; the averaged letters (d = -h/2) lie OUTSIDE rho(B_3), so the element is not in the image of rho and carries no crossing number, volume or genus -- tr_M of it is by linearity a weighted sum of 2^(2A+1) link invariants, not the invariant of one link (producer docstring, PR #5765).

[RECOMPUTED 2026-08-31 on the CANONICAL 11-letter element (bean qou-1ucq, probe computations/markov/assembly_chain_11_letter_recompute_probe.py, 7/7). This step previously evaluated chi from a LEGACY word -- a 6-crossing word asserted to be ALL POSITIVE sigma -- which is a different element of H_3(q) from the one atom_braid_word_3A returns. The canonical element has 11 letters: 6 sigma (d = 0), 3 sigma^-1 (d = -h), 2 averaged (d = -h/2). Each letter (c, d, g) denotes the Hecke element c*sigma_g + d*1, so chi^lambda is the trace of the seminormal matrix product with sigma_g -> rho^lambda(sigma_g) and the averaged letters acting as rho^lambda(sigma_g) - (q - q^-1)/2 * 1. That is the only route the producer's own docstring permits: no crossing number may be read off this object.]
steps.notes: 1-dim rep; under the LEGACY 6-letter σ-word convention (T_w_p = σ_1 σ_2 σ_1 σ_2 σ_1 σ_2, all positive, n_+=6, n_-=0) χ^(3)_q(T_w_p) = q^6.  CAVEAT: under the CANONICAL convention from `atomic-braid-recipe-p.derivation.json` (11 crossings = 6 σ + 3 σ^{-1} + 2 averaged), the same trivial rep evaluates differently: each averaged crossing (σ − h/2·1) acts as (q + q^{-1})/2 on the trivial rep (from σ ↦ +q ⇒ σ − h/2 ↦ q − (q − q^{-1})/2 = (q + q^{-1})/2), and each σ^{-1} acts as q^{-1}.  The two conventions therefore give different symbolic χ^(3) values; the chain leaf at q_0 is hardcoded against TR_M_AT_Q0 (canonical numerics via markov_trace_symbolic), so this legacy-convention monomial is illustrative. steps.name: Hoefsmit rep χ^(2,1)_q on proton braid word
steps.operation:
Reference the existing `hoefsmit-rep-21-sigma1.derivation.json` chain for ρ^(2,1)(σ_1).  ρ^(2,1)(σ_2) is obtained by the same Hoefsmit recipe applied to the σ_2 generator: the recipe depends only on the cell adjacency between i and i+1 in each SYT (which is intrinsic to the partition shape, not to the specific generator index), so ρ^(2,1)(σ_2) = ρ^(2,1)(σ_1)' where the prime denotes the SYT-basis automorphism that swaps the role of i=1, i+1=2 with i=2, i+1=3.  Concretely for λ=(2,1): the two SYT (T_1=[1 2 / 3], T_2=[1 3 / 2]) have the same cell-adjacency profile under the σ_1 ↔ σ_2 swap, so the matrix entries are identical (after relabelling T_1, T_2).  Extend by braid-word matrix multiplication to T_w_p (six σ-crossings alternating σ_1, σ_2); χ^(2,1)_q(T_w_p) is the trace of the 2x2 matrix product.

steps.name: Finite-Jones Markov-trace assembly
steps.operation:
tr_M(T_w_p, q) = w_(3)(q) · χ^(3)_q(T_w_p) + w_(2,1)(q) · χ^(2,1)_q(T_w_p) + w_(1,1,1)(q) · χ^(1,1,1)_q(T_w_p).  Uniqueness of this assembly is the **finite-Jones** axiom: Markov stabilisation tr_M(α σ_n) = z · tr_M(α) determines the trace uniquely on the closure of every braid word.
